advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish 'no per-model series listed' from 'checked and genuinely zero' in _metered_spend so an empty/transient listing cannot release an active deny.
evidence: handler.py:338: `if not found_series:`
handler.py:340: `return float(0)`
`found_series` is only set True inside the list_metrics loop (handler.py:298); an empty page or a region whose metrics briefly do not list leaves it False
Main gate at handler.py:562 `if any_attached and spend < THRESHOLD_USD and not signal_unavailable:` treats metered==0.0 as available and releases the deny
Ticket 8d27 final comment: '_metered_spend still cannot distinguish genuinely zero usage from missing per-model series' — acknowledged advisory shipping in this diff
advisory.finding: _metered_spend returns 0.0 when no per-ModelId series is found (found_series stays False), which is indistinguishable from a transient/empty list_metrics page. The main gate treats this 0.0 as a real available zero-spend signal and can RELEASE an active deny policy — a fail-open of the release path when the producer merely emitted nothing.
scenarios: A day with real spend where list_metrics transiently returns no ModelId series while a deny is attached: the deny is released even though spend continues

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make _metered_spend degrade per-region rather than discarding already-summed totals when one region errors.
evidence: handler.py:281: `total = float(0)` accumulates across the `for region in REGIONS:` loop
handler.py:316-318: `except ClientError ... return None` (list path)
handler.py:329-331: `except ClientError ... return None` (data path)
Ticket 8d27 links cilium-embolic-mantaray: 'one region ClientError discards token totals already collected from healthy regions, converting a partial poll into a declared full metering outage'
advisory.finding: In _metered_spend, a ClientError from list_metrics or get_metric_data in ANY region returns None, discarding token totals already accumulated from earlier healthy regions — a partial poll is reported as a full metering outage.
scenarios: us-east-1 returns real spend, then us-west-2 GetMetricData throws: the us-east-1 total is thrown away and the tick sees metered=None

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard CE response parsing in _ce_spend_today/_refresh_rates so a malformed-but-successful response does not abort the tick with an uncaught KeyError.
evidence: handler.py:361: `return float(results[0]["Total"]["UnblendedCost"]["Amount"])`
handler.py:349-350 in _refresh_rates: `cost = float(group["Metrics"]["UnblendedCost"]["Amount"])` etc.
Callers only catch ClientError: handler.py:494-505 (`except ClientError`) and handler.py:469-474
Ticket 8d27 comment lists '_ce_spend_today still assumes a present Total object when results exist' as an intentionally-skipped advisory
advisory.finding: _ce_spend_today and _refresh_rates index CE response keys directly ('Total','UnblendedCost','Amount','UsageQuantity'); a missing key raises KeyError (not ClientError), which escapes the caller's `except ClientError` handlers and aborts the entire tick, disabling enforcement, release, and state persistence.
scenarios: CE returns a result period with no Total (e.g. filtered-empty shape variation): KeyError propagates out of handler and the whole 5-minute tick dies

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Validate/guard ce_last_poll parsing (fromisoformat) so a corrupt timestamp field cannot abort every tick.
evidence: handler.py:489: `or (now - dt.datetime.fromisoformat(last_poll)).total_seconds() >= CE_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`
_load_state guards only json.loads / ClientError: handler.py at `except (ClientError, ValueError)` returns {} for parse failure, but a valid-JSON dict with a bad ce_last_poll string passes through
This fromisoformat call is not wrapped in try/except in the handler
advisory.finding: The main handler calls dt.datetime.fromisoformat(state.get('ce_last_poll')) but _load_state only validates that the parameter is JSON, not that individual fields are well-formed; a corrupt/non-isoformat ce_last_poll raises ValueError in the handler body (outside any try), aborting the tick.
scenarios: A state blob that is valid JSON but has ce_last_poll set to a non-timestamp string (manual edit, older format) makes every tick raise ValueError until state is cleared

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive the Logs and State IAM resource ARNs from var.aws_region (or data.aws_region.current) rather than a hardcoded "us-east-1", or pin the Lambda/clients to us-east-1 explicitly.
evidence: infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf:296-300 log-group ARN uses literal "us-east-1"
infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf:317-322 SSM parameter ARN uses literal "us-east-1"
provider region is var.aws_region (default us-east-1): infra/terraform/main.tf:5-7 and infra/terraform/variables.tf:1-5
handler creates ssm/iam/cloudwatch clients with no explicit region: handler.py `ssm = boto3.client("ssm")`, `iam = boto3.client("iam")` — these bind to the Lambda's region, not necessarily us-east-1
advisory.finding: The Lambda execution IAM policy hardcodes the region to us-east-1 for the Logs and State (SSM parameter) resource ARNs, but the Lambda function and its boto3 clients (ssm, cloudwatch default, iam) run in the provider region var.aws_region. If var.aws_region is ever changed from its us-east-1 default, the Lambda will attempt to write logs and read/write its state SSM parameter in the deployment region while the policy only permits us-east-1, causing AccessDenied — enforcement silently stops.
scenarios: Someone sets var.aws_region to a non-us-east-1 value; the whole stack moves region but the spend-cap Lambda loses log/state permissions and stops enforcing.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the literal "us-east-1" in the Logs and State statement ARNs with var.aws_region (matching the provider), and set region_name explicitly on the handler's ssm/iam/cloudwatch clients so the policy and runtime regions cannot diverge.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Give aws_budgets_budget.bedrock_daily a stable name (e.g. "bedrock-daily-cap") independent of the cap value so changing the threshold is an in-place update.
evidence: infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf:215 `name = format("bedrock-daily-%s", var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd)`
budget also sets `limit_amount = tostring(var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd)` at line 217, so the amount is already captured without needing it in the name
advisory.finding: The alert-only budget resource name embeds the dollar cap value via format("bedrock-daily-%s", var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd), so any change to bedrock_daily_cap_usd renames the budget and forces a destroy-and-recreate of aws_budgets_budget.bedrock_daily rather than an in-place update.
scenarios: Operator raises/lowers the cap via bedrock_daily_cap_usd; the budget is torn down and recreated, briefly leaving no budget alerting during apply.
advisory.suggested_fix: Set name = "bedrock-daily-cap" (or similar constant); limit_amount already conveys the value.

evidence: bedrock_spend_cap.tf:295-299 `Resource = format("arn:aws:logs:%s:%s:log-group:/aws/lambda/%s:*", "us-east-1", ...)`
bedrock_spend_cap.tf:317-322 `format("arn:aws:ssm:%s:%s:parameter/%s/state", "us-east-1", ...)`
main.tf:5-7 `provider "aws" { region = var.aws_region }`
variables.tf:1-5 `variable "aws_region" { ... default = "us-east-1" }`
The aws_cloudwatch_log_group and aws_lambda_function set no region override, so they inherit var.aws_region while the IAM ARNs are pinned to a literal us-east-1.
advisory.finding: The Lambda's IAM policy hardcodes region "us-east-1" in the Logs and State ARNs (and the handler hardcodes region_name="us-east-1" for the ce client), but the AWS provider deploys the Lambda, log group, and SSM parameter into var.aws_region (default us-east-1). If var.aws_region is overridden to any non-us-east-1 region, the Lambda and its log group are created in that region while the IAM grant references log-group and parameter ARNs in us-east-1, so logging (logs:CreateLogGroup/PutLogEvents) and SSM state read/write are denied, and enforcement silently stops.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the literal "us-east-1" in the Logs and State ARN format() calls with var.aws_region (or data.aws_region.current.name), and align the handler's REGIONS/ce region with the same source.

evidence: bedrock_spend_cap.tf:215 `name = format("bedrock-daily-%s", var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd)`
bedrock_spend_cap.tf:217 `limit_amount = tostring(var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd)` already carries the cap value, so encoding it in the name too couples the immutable name to a routinely-tuned input.
README.md guidance: "**Change the cap:** set `bedrock_daily_cap_usd` and apply." — the documented normal operation triggers a destroy/recreate of the alerting budget.
advisory.finding: The DAILY budget resource name embeds the cap dollar value: name = format("bedrock-daily-%s", var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd). aws_budgets_budget.name is immutable, so changing bedrock_daily_cap_usd forces Terraform to destroy and recreate the budget rather than update it in place. On a live cost-control tripwire this deletes the existing budget (and its notification history) and briefly leaves no alerting budget during the replace.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change name to a constant like format("bedrock-daily") or "bedrock-daily-cap"; keep the dollar value only in limit_amount.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm denying Bedrock to the whole Admin IAM group on a trip is the intended blast radius, and document/limit it if not.
evidence: infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf:100 `default     = ["Admin"]`
README notes the deny is invocation-only so admins can still lift it, but the attachment is account-wide across all Admin members
dropped.finding: The IAM 'Admin' group is included as a deny target (bedrock_cap_target_groups default ["Admin"]), so when the daily cap trips the deny policy is attached to the entire admin group — denying Bedrock invocation to every human administrator, a very large blast radius.
scenarios: A runaway trips the cap; all admins lose Bedrock invocation simultaneously until 00:00 UTC or manual detach, even those uninvolved in the runaway.

variable "bedrock_warn_threshold_usd" and "bedrock_cap_unknown_rate_per_1k" similarly have no validation

dropped.finding: The core operational variables bedrock_daily_cap_usd, bedrock_warn_threshold_usd, bedrock_cap_seed_rates and bedrock_cap_unknown_rate_per_1k have no defaults and no validation blocks, so a misconfigured or non-positive cap (e.g. 0 or a warn threshold above the cap) is accepted with no plan-time guard.
